request: Add two horizontal buttons to the front panel. One above existing one, the other below - all approximately equally distanced. Buttons should be copies of existing one.

actions.operation: Copy/duplicate existing button feature to create a new button instance on the front panel

parameters.spacing: approximately equal distance relative to the other buttons

actions.target: Existing button (source geometry) on the front panel
actions.relational_constraint: Place the copied button above the existing button on the front panel; keep it horizontal; align with existing button such that spacing is approximately equal among the three buttons (top, existing/middle, bottom).
actions.unresolved_reference: The model.json does not explicitly label the existing front-panel horizontal button with a face_code. Based on multiview imagery, the likely source is the single horizontal pill-shaped button on the left side of the front control panel near the dial (within S6 minor faces FACE 419-451). Final identification requires selecting that pill-shaped button solid/feature in CAD and confirming its mating face is on the front-facing control panel surface.
steps: Localize the edit region: use the multiview ("top" image showing the appliance front) to identify the existing single horizontal pill-shaped button left of the rotary dial. In the model, this button is most likely one of the small control/indicator solids captured under S6 minor faces (Brep FACE 419-451) because S6 explicitly includes small local features near the dial cluster.

Establish the front-panel reference plane for placement/alignment: select the front-facing reference face of the housing in the control area. If an explicit outer front control-panel face is not separately labeled, use S1 face_code 0004 (Brep FACE 11, front-facing normal ≈ -Y) as the primary front-direction reference, then create an offset datum plane to the actual outer skin/control face as needed (offset distance = measured thickness between FACE 11 and the exterior control surface).

Identify the source button feature/body: select the existing horizontal pill button solid (or the feature that created it) by picking its largest outward-facing planar/near-planar face and its surrounding blend faces; confirm it lies on/flush with the front control surface and is oriented with its long axis horizontal (left-right). Record its placement reference (button center point and long-axis direction).

Create a vertical placement direction: define a construction axis in global +Z (vertical) passing through the existing button center. (+Z is consistent with the model z-range [0..~320] and with the visual vertical direction in the front control-panel view.)

Define equal spacing (pitch): measure the available vertical clearance on the front control panel for a 3-button stack (top clearance to nearest top boundary/fillet or nearby control features, and bottom clearance to the next boundary/feature). Set pitch so that the three button centerlines are equally spaced: pitch = (Z_top_limit - Z_bottom_limit) / 2, where Z_top_limit and Z_bottom_limit are chosen to maintain the same edge/feature clearance as the existing middle button (use the existing middle button’s clearance as the design intent).

Duplicate the button: perform a Move/Copy Body (or Pattern Feature if the button is a parametric feature) of the identified existing horizontal button. Translation vector = +pitch * Ẑ (upward). Keep X and Y positions identical to the existing button so the three buttons are vertically aligned in a column and remain on the same front control surface.

Boolean/assembly behavior: if the button is modeled as a separate solid cap, keep it as a separate solid/component consistent with the existing one; if it is modeled as a boss feature integrated into a panel solid, merge/boolean-union the copied boss into the same parent body as the original (typically the control panel/housing body).

Verify: confirm the new (upper) button remains horizontal, is flush/mated to the front control surface, does not intersect the rotary dial assembly (S6 major faces 0037-0043) and maintains similar edge radii/fillets as the source button.

steps: Reuse the same source button identification and the same front-panel reference plane/datum plane established for the upper-button action (S6 minor faces likely contain the existing button; S1 face_code 0004 provides a stable front-direction reference).
Reuse the same vertical construction axis through the existing button center (global +Z).

Reuse the same pitch definition used to place the upper button so spacing is equal among all three. (Do not independently dimension the lower copy; drive both upper and lower offsets with the same pitch parameter to preserve equal spacing when the design changes.)

Duplicate the button: perform Move/Copy Body (or Pattern Feature) of the existing horizontal button with translation vector = -pitch * Ẑ (downward). Keep X and Y positions identical to the existing button so all three are vertically aligned and remain on the same front control surface.

Boolean/assembly behavior: match the original modeling intent—separate solid/component if the original is separate; boolean-union into the same parent body if the original is a boss/feature integrated into the panel.

Edge/finish continuity: ensure the lower copy inherits the same corner radii/fillets/chamfers as the original button. If the original button is seated in a recess (cut), pattern/copy the recess-cut feature as well to maintain the same fit and flushness.

Verify: check for interference with the cavity opening region (S1 cavity ceiling/inner roof face_code 0005 and nearby inner frame geometry) and ensure the lower button stays on the front control-panel region rather than crossing into the open cavity boundary. Confirm equal center-to-center spacing between (top, middle) and (middle, bottom).

intention: Add two additional front-panel buttons by replicating the existing button, creating a vertically arranged set with roughly equal spacing.
